b: We went and saw some old church.. You can see more beautiful churches than that back home.. There's a big, beautiful church near the Modara temple…

After that we went to a place called Note Café..,Five floors… all covered in those little coloured sticky papers you stick in exercise books.. Apparently people who've had coffee can write something for those they like and stick it up before they leave… They don't tear them down… They were stuck on everything, walls, ceiling, lights.. In my school, too, they'd write all sorts in the bathroom… Seems they want to pass the time even while they're going… Seems someone stole the idea from there and set up a shop like this…

So we bought coffee and wrote and stuck notes too… I proudly wrote and stuck up "Tamil will win", thinking like Kalaignar.. Then we wrote and stuck some for our friends… One of us, like a monkey, said he'd stick his on the ceiling and somehow wrote and stuck it there… Let's trust the shop will still be there when we come back to read them.. Because that's our kind of luck (I'll tell you in detail in another chapter)

After that we went to see Ho Chi Minh's tomb… Communist leader… Red everywhere you looked dazzled the eyes.. And while sending us in, an army lady hit Thushara, telling her to move faster… Since we arrived we've been getting hit; I thought some big blow was coming somewhere.. With the anger Thushara had, we'd all have ended up in jail… Luckily her anger died down

After that, having seen something called the One Pillar Pagoda with complete satisfaction, we set off madly searching for an Indian restaurant; they'd all joined me, saying they couldn't eat any more without salt or spice… But nothing in the food had any heat or masala .. it was a letdown

When we finished that and came back to the room, the whole street was a market .. It happens Saturday and Sunday nights apparently.. Terribly cheap… We'll catch here what we missed there, we said, and bought heaps of things.. Ice cream that makes smoke come out of your mouth, clothes, wooden things, we bought it all, went to the room and slept
The next day, another bus journey
note: Kalaignar is M. Karunanidhi, the Tamil Nadu leader and writer, whose slogan was "Tamil will win". The Modara church is in the north of Colombo.
